result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Neither answer invents outcomes or guarantees, and both use clearly marked testimonial placeholders. A builds trust more fully and honestly: it records a baseline at the first visit, re-checks the same measures, gives honest timelines and mentions imaging or referral. Its About blurb also includes every fact, including the $95 price. B is solid but thinner, leaves the price out of the About blurb, and its 'opened five weeks ago' line will go stale on a live page. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers avoid invented outcomes and guarantees, and both mark testimonial slots clearly as placeholders while covering all the real facts. B builds trust more concretely for a new clinic: it sets a baseline at assessment, re-checks the same measures, gives honest timelines and says when it would refer someone on, and it adds a useful note on regulator rules. A is tighter but gives less detail on how progress is shown. B adds a little invented backstory ('we started Northgate because...') and an opening disclaimer the client didn't need, but these are minor.
